blanks.sentence: At first, the new surroundings took one woman outside her familiar _____.
Living and working in another country brought _____, including unfamiliar local foods.
Some _____ from her previous cooking were unavailable.
The second woman moved from England to the Caribbean island of _____.
Seasoning was an _____ part of preparing food there.
Individual cooks made their own small _____.
There were no set _____ for the seasoning.
With no fixed quantities, learning involved _____: trying different methods and learning from mistakes, some of which her family did not appreciate.

multipleChoice.question: What broad difficulty can arise when people move to another country?
options: They may have to give up cooking familiar dishes entirely.
They may need to adjust to food that differs from what they know.
They may find that local people reject food from abroad.
They may struggle to learn the names of local dishes.

multipleChoice.question: What led the first woman to leave Ukraine?
options: An invitation to open a restaurant abroad.
A wish to train with Dutch cooks.
A plan to join relatives in Poland.
The Russian invasion of her country.

multipleChoice.question: What contrast does she draw between staying in one place and moving abroad?
options: Familiar routines give way to situations that require adjustment.
Familiar ingredients become easier to obtain after a move.
Working abroad removes the difficulties of daily life.
Moving abroad makes cooking less important than before.

multipleChoice.question: How did she respond when some ingredients from home were unavailable?
options: She stopped preparing her usual kinds of meals.
She ordered the missing ingredients from Ukraine.
She found local substitutes and cooked with what she had.
She asked her customers to choose replacement ingredients.

multipleChoice.question: How did customers respond to the cooking she developed in the Netherlands?
options: They rejected it because it used unfamiliar ingredients.
They enjoyed the new kind of cooking she created.
They insisted that she restore every original recipe.
They welcomed it only after she imported Ukrainian staples.

multipleChoice.question: Why are the small personal adjustments to seasoning relevant?
options: They show that cooks develop individual ways of flavouring food.
They show that cooks normally measure every spice precisely.
They show that food preparation is identical across families.
They show that the newcomer rejected local cooking methods.

multipleChoice.question: What wider conclusion is supported by the two food experiences?
options: Successful adaptation requires people to abandon foods from home.
Food customs are easier to learn than other parts of a culture.
Encountering local food can reveal how people live and cook.
A new culture can be understood only by opening a restaurant.
